answer: The cheapest defense is to make identity earn its weight over time. Each new identity needs two sponsors from separate standing neighborhoods, both listed in the timber registry. Sponsors lock collateral in the terrace pool that is seized if a random audit finds the recruit's work copied or empty. First rewards stay escrowed in the cedar ledger until three unrelated peers verify a real task receipt. A farm cannot bootstrap itself: N fake identities require N independent sponsors with clean histories and money at risk, so headcount carries a capital cost, not just a registration fee.
